test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 15 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following organ can be donated while the donor is alive?

I. Part of a liver

II. Kidney
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Living organ donation** allows healthy individuals to donate certain organs or tissues while they are alive to save or enhance the lives of others. This is regulated under strict medical guidelines and ethical considerations.
 
• Part of a liver can be donated by a living donor. The liver has a unique ability to regenerate, making it possible for a portion of the liver to be transplanted while the donor’s liver regrows to its normal size. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• A kidney can be donated by a living donor. Humans typically have two kidneys, and one kidney is sufficient for a donor to live a healthy life while the donated kidney can save the life of the recipient. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• Living organ donation is strictly regulated to ensure the safety of both the donor and the recipient. It requires comprehensive medical evaluations and legal consent processes.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Organ Donation:**

 
 
• Organ donation refers to the process of donating organs or tissues from a donor to a recipient. It can be done either after death (cadaveric donation) or by living donors.
 
• Living donors can donate organs like kidneys, part of the liver, or tissues such as bone marrow, provided they meet strict medical criteria.
 
• Organ donations save lives, especially in cases of chronic organ failure such as kidney or liver failure.
 
 
 
• **Liver Donation:**
 
 
• The liver is the only organ in the human body capable of regenerating itself. This allows living donors to donate a portion of their liver, which regrows to its normal size in both the donor and the recipient.
 
• Liver donation typically involves removing either the right or left lobe of the liver, depending on the size and needs of the recipient.
 
• Regeneration usually takes place within a few months of donation.
 
 
 
• **Kidney Donation:**
 
 
• Kidneys are vital for filtering waste and maintaining fluid balance in the body. Living individuals with healthy kidney function can donate one kidney.
 
• A kidney transplant is often the best treatment for end-stage renal disease (ESRD) or chronic kidney failure.
 
• Donors undergo extensive medical evaluations to ensure their remaining kidney can sustain normal kidney function.
 
 
 
• **Legal and Ethical Guidelines:**
 
 
• Organ donation is regulated under laws such as the **Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994,** in India, which ensures ethical practices and prohibits organ trafficking.
 
• Donors must give informed consent, and medical professionals must ensure donors are not coerced or exploited.
 
• Both donor and recipient undergo psychological and medical evaluations to ensure a safe and ethical transplant process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for Living Donation:**

 
 
• Donors must be in good physical and mental health, typically between the ages of **18 and 60 years**.
 
• They must undergo rigorous medical tests, including blood tests, imaging scans, and psychological assessments.
 
• Living donors are often family members or close relatives of the recipient to reduce the risk of organ rejection.
 
 
 
• **Statistics:**
 
 
• Globally, living organ donation accounts for a significant portion of transplants. For example, in **India**, about **90% of kidney transplants** come from living donors.
 
• Countries like the **United States** and **South Korea** also see high rates of living donation, particularly for kidney and liver transplants.
 
 
 
• **Awareness Campaigns:**
 
 
• Initiatives like **National Organ Donation Day** (celebrated annually on **27th November** in India) aim to educate the public about the life-saving benefits of organ donation.
